steps.observation: You have 30 seconds. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action: A transformer processes a sequence of token embeddings plus positional encodings through repeated “self-attention” and feed-forward layers. In self-attention, each token computes a weighted sum of all other tokens’ representations—so it dynamically “attends” to whatever positions matter for the task. Multiple attention heads let it look at different aspects in parallel. In encoder-decoder models (like for translation), the encoder stack builds context, and the decoder stack uses both self-attention (on previous outputs) and cross-attention (on the encoder’s outputs) before projecting to next-token probabilities. Because there’s no recurrence, it can be highly parallel and scale to very large models.
